Devices.title: Devices
Devices.explanation: A device with a key may send recipes to your inbox without signing in. One key per device, so a lost phone only means revoking one key.
Devices.secretWarning: It is shown once and never again. Put it into the Shortcut now.
Devices.setupIntro: iOS will not put a website in the share sheet, so a shortcut does it. Built once, then it is one tap from Safari, Instagram, YouTube, Photos or Notes. The steps name the English Shortcuts app; other languages use the same actions.
Devices.sc1Intro: The one you use 95% of the time: share a recipe page, done.
Devices.sc1Step1: Shortcuts app → “+”. Tap the name at the top and rename it, for example “Save To Moscookbook”.
Devices.sc1Step2: Add the action “Get Contents of URL”, expand it (the blue arrow on the right) and set:
Devices.sc1Step3: For the “url” field, tap the value and pick the blue “Shortcut Input” variable from above the keyboard. Typed text does not work — it has to be the variable.
Devices.sc1Step4: A bar now appears at the top by itself: “Receive Any input from Share Sheet”. Tap “Any” and turn off everything except URLs and Text. If the bar does not appear, tap “ⓘ” at the bottom and turn on “Show in Share Sheet”.
Devices.sc1Step5: Test it: open a recipe in Safari, share, scroll down, pick the shortcut. It should be in the inbox within seconds.
Devices.sc2Intro: For Instagram, cookbook pages in your library, and anything that cannot be read any other way. Several pages are joined into one picture.
Devices.sc2Step1: New shortcut. First action “Combine Images”, Mode “Vertically”, Spacing 0, with “Shortcut Input” as its input — that turns several selected screenshots into one tall picture.
Devices.sc2Step2: “Convert Image”, format JPEG, input “Combined Image”. Turn “Preserve Metadata” off, or your photos' GPS coordinates travel with them.
Devices.sc2Step3: “Base64 Encode” with “Converted Image” as its input.
Devices.sc2Step4: “Get Contents of URL” — address, method and header as in the first shortcut, but the body is a dictionary called “image” with two fields:
Devices.sc2Step5: In the bar at the top, leave only “Images” on. Then pick one or more pictures in Photos, share, choose the shortcut.
Devices.sc2Note: With no AI key the picture is still kept and the inbox says what is missing. Nothing is ever rejected for want of a key. Two to four pages are fine; beyond that the picture gets so tall that the text is illegible once it is scaled down.
Devices.sc3Intro: Optional. Saves two taps over “take a photo, then share it”.
Devices.sc3Step1: New shortcut, no share sheet. Actions in this order: “Take Photo”, then “Base64 Encode”, then “Get Contents of URL”. The order is the most common mistake — encoding happens before sending.
Devices.sc3Step2: Expand “Take Photo” and leave “Show Camera Preview” on, or it fires blind.
Devices.sc3Step3: “Get Contents of URL” takes the same body as the second shortcut.
Devices.sc3Step4: To run it: long-press the shortcut → “Share” → “Add to Home Screen”. Faster still: Settings → Accessibility → Touch → Back Tap.
Devices.troubleIntro: Add “Quick Look” as the last action and the shortcut shows you the server's answer.
Devices.trouble401aA: The header is not named exactly “Authorization”, or the “Bearer ” prefix with its space is missing.
Devices.trouble401bQ: 401 That capture token is not valid
Devices.trouble401bA: Key mis-copied or revoked. Create a new one above.
Devices.trouble400Q: 400 Send a url, some text, or both
Devices.trouble400A: The “url” field holds typed text instead of the blue “Shortcut Input” variable.
Devices.trouble413Q: 413 That is too large to capture
Devices.trouble413A: The request is over 4 MB, more than the server accepts. Resize the screenshots before sending (“Resize Image” to 1200 px, JPEG) or send fewer.
Devices.troubleSilentA: Usually the order of the actions: encoding has to happen before sending, not after.
Devices.queuedNote: The reply now only says that something arrived; the reading happens afterwards. The shortcut used to wait for the page to be fetched, parsed and, if needed, read by a model, which on one recipe page was a measured fifteen seconds with the phone in your hand.
Devices.sc2Link1: In Instagram, tap Share → “Copy link” on the post, then take the screenshot.
Devices.sc2Link2: In the screenshot shortcut, add the action “Get Clipboard” before “Get Contents of URL”.
Devices.sc2Link3: In the request body's dictionary, add a text field “url” and choose the blue variable “Clipboard” as its value:
Devices.sc2LinkNote: The link and the screenshot then arrive together: the post is read first – its caption, and a recipe link in it is followed – and the screenshot is the picture, and the fallback if that is not enough. If the clipboard does not hold a link, it is ignored.
Devices.sc1ShotsTitle: With the latest screenshots (post, comments, bio)
Devices.sc1ShotsIntro: If you share a post and took screenshots just before – of the comment with the recipe, or the link in the bio – the shortcut sends up to 3 of them along. The AI reads them together in one call and follows links and websites shown on them. Without new screenshots only the link is sent, as before.
Devices.sc1Shots1: At the very top (before “Get Contents of URL”): “Adjust Date” – “Current Date”, “Subtract” 5 “minutes”.
Devices.sc1Shots2: “Find Photos”: filter “Is a Screenshot” and “Date Taken” “is after” “Adjusted Date”. “Sort by” “Date Taken”, “Order” “Latest First”, “Limit” on, “Get” 3 Photos.
Devices.sc1Shots4: Inside it “Repeat with Each” over “Photos”. Inside the repeat: “Resize Image” to width 1200 (auto height), then “Convert Image” to JPEG, quality about 70%, “Preserve Metadata” off, then “Base64 Encode” (under “Show More”: “Line Breaks” set to “None”).
Devices.sc1Shots5: After “End Repeat” (still inside the “If”): “Combine Text” with “Repeat Results”, separator “Custom” and a comma “,”.
Devices.sc1Shots6: Then “Get Contents of URL” as above, but with two text fields in the request body:
Devices.sc1Shots7: Under “Otherwise” the existing “Get Contents of URL” with only “url” stays.
Devices.sc1ShotsNote: The order of the screenshots does not matter. Resizing matters: Vercel accepts at most about 4 MB per request; three screenshots 1200 px wide come to about 1 MB.

Legal.purposeValue: A private collection of recipes. No commercial activity, no advertising, no paid links.
Legal.imprintBasis: Disclosure under § 25 (5) of the Austrian Media Act. The site pursues no commercial purpose, so § 5 of the E-Commerce Act does not apply. Should that change — through advertising or affiliate links, say — an address able to receive official post and further details have to be added here.
Legal.privacyIntro: This site is a private collection of recipes. There are no analytics, no advertising, no embedded fonts and no third-party scripts. There is correspondingly little to explain.
Legal.controllerBody: Moritz Schumacher, Vienna, reachable at moscookbook@gmail.com. Questions about your data are answered at that address.
Legal.whatDataBody: With an account: a first and last name, an e-mail address, and a password kept only as a bcrypt hash. If you set up a passkey, also its public key and a device label such as “iPhone · Safari” – the private key never leaves your device. Plus whatever you enter yourself — ratings, cooking notes, photographs you upload. Without an account: only the technical data that fetching a page produces.
Legal.whyBody: Only to run the cookbook: to sign you in, to attribute your contributions to the right person, and to send you a link if you need to reset your password. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, and for keeping the accounts and preventing abuse also (f).
Legal.cookiesBody: Exactly one: an encrypted session cookie that keeps you signed in. It is strictly necessary, so it needs no consent, and it does not follow you beyond this site. There is no consent banner because there is nothing to consent to.
Legal.processorsBody: Vercel (hosting and image storage), Neon (the database, in the Frankfurt region) and Google (sending the few e-mails, through a Gmail account). That is the whole list.
Legal.retentionBody: Accounts and contributions stay until you ask for them to go. Password reset links expire after an hour. Counters against too many requests hold an IP address for a few minutes and are then swept. The error log records a path and a message, and neither an IP address nor an account.
Legal.rightsBody: You may ask for access, correction, deletion, restriction and portability of your data, and you may object to its processing. Writing to me is enough. If you would like to complain, the Austrian Data Protection Authority in Vienna is the place.
Legal.privacyUpdated: As of September 2026. If something on the site changes that is described here, this text changes with it.

Ai.title: AI import
Ai.intro: Recipes are read with rules first — structured data on the page, a video's description, pasted text. That costs nothing and works without any of this. A key is the second attempt: for a photograph, because pixels have no rule, and for the many blogs that write their ingredients with no markup at all.
Ai.cannotStore: This installation has no session secret to seal a key under. Until SECRET_COOKIE_PASSWORD is set, nothing can be stored here.
Ai.modeIntro: The rules run first in every setting. This only says whether anything is asked afterwards.
Ai.modeHelp_off: Rules only. Stored keys sit unused — photographs land in the inbox with the picture and wait for you.
Ai.modeHelp_images: Only where there is no rule: a photograph of a cookbook page, a screenshot. Everything else stays rule-based and free.

Ai.stylePlaceholder: e.g. address the reader directly, short sentences, don't repeat amounts in the steps, fan oven temperatures.
Ai.proxyTitle: Fetch blocked pages through a reading service
Ai.proxyExplain: Some recipe sites (e.g. maangchi.com) refuse every server. The cookbook then asks once more through the reading service r.jina.ai, which sees that page's address. Switched off, such a page lands in the inbox as “could not be read”.
Ai.smallFirstTitle: Read recipes from text with the small model first
Ai.smallFirstExplain: A small model (e.g. Claude Haiku) costs a fraction per token and is enough for most recipes. When its answer is incomplete – ingredients with no method, a title and nothing else – the configured model reads the same again. Photos are always read by the configured model. “Usage” shows which model was needed how often.

SiteProfiles.title: Learned sites
SiteProfiles.intro: The first import from an unknown site teaches the cookbook where that site puts its recipe. Every later import from it needs no AI. This list fills itself — you are only here to teach a site in advance, or to correct one that has gone out of date. Only recipe websites are learned, and only when the page has no recipe markup and the AI helped. Instagram, TikTok and YouTube have no fixed page layout and do not appear here. Instead the cookbook remembers which website an account keeps its recipes on (“pattyplates.com (link in bio)”) and looks the dish up there on the next post – usually without AI.
SiteProfiles.none: Nothing learned yet. That happens on the next import from a website without recipe markup where the AI helped. Photos from a cookbook never appear here: a photo has no address to remember a page layout under – it is read afresh every time.
SiteProfiles.stale: Set aside: three imports in a row fell short. The next import will learn the site again.
SiteProfiles.failures: {count, plural, one {# recent import} other {# recent imports}} below the threshold.
SiteProfiles.sourcesIntro: Every source of your imports, and why something was or was not learned for it.
SiteProfiles.sourceCount: {count, plural, one {# import} other {# imports}} · {rules} without AI · {ai} with AI
SiteProfiles.whyLearned: Learned: further imports from here need no AI.
SiteProfiles.whyMarkup: Read without AI – the page describes its recipe itself (recipe markup). There is nothing to learn; imports from here already cost nothing.
SiteProfiles.whyNotYet: The AI read it, but the site is not learned yet (learning could not reproduce the result). You can try again here.
SiteProfiles.why_photo: Photos, e.g. from a cookbook: a photo has no page layout to remember – each is read by the AI. That is by design for books, not a fault.
SiteProfiles.why_instagram: No fixed page layout. What is remembered instead is the website where an account keeps its recipes.
SiteProfiles.why_tiktok: No fixed page layout. What is remembered instead is the website where an account keeps its recipes.
SiteProfiles.why_youtube: Videos: read from the description and subtitles, with no page layout to learn.
SiteProfiles.why_note: Pasted text: read by rules or by the AI; a text has no layout to learn.
SiteProfiles.whyOther: There is no page layout to learn here.

Drafts.title: Drafts
Drafts.intro: Recipes that have been imported and tidied up but are not yet yours. They appear nowhere else — not in the list, not in search, not as a suggestion, never in public, and no post can be written about one. Cook it once, adjust it, then finish it.
Drafts.none: No drafts. From the inbox you can put a recipe here as a draft instead of adding it to the cookbook straight away.
Drafts.banner: This is a draft. It is not in your list, cannot be found by searching, and cannot be made public or shared.
Drafts.stageHint: Takes the recipe in, but not yet into your list.

Work.notePlaceholder: What should the AI do or look out for? (optional)
Work.publicHint: Goes onto the public task list, anonymised — without names, e-mail addresses or links with keys.
Work.explain: Tasks for an AI, or whoever you have working on the code. The list is under Reports → Tasks. On it by itself: every error the server sees or a signed-in person runs into. You add tickets ("Have AI implement it", your own also straight away with “Straight to the AI”) and inbox items ("Have AI improve reading this"). When a task is done, the AI reports it — it then sits there at the top under “Done by the AI – please confirm”, and your tap closes it along with its error or ticket. If an error happens again afterwards, the task reopens by itself. The list is public and anonymised at this address; the brief for the AI is in the repository at docs/work-list-prompt.md.
Work.empty: No tasks. Errors are added by themselves; tickets and inbox items you add with the button on each – or write a ticket with “Straight to the AI”.

Work.shareExplainCapture: Goes onto the task list: an AI finds out why this item was read badly and improves the reading. Once you confirm, it is read again.
Work.shareExplainError: Goes onto the task list: an AI finds the cause and fixes it.
Work.sharedDone: AI reports it done – confirm under Tasks
Work.awaitingHeading: Done by the AI – please confirm
Work.tokenExplain: An AI uses it to report a task done. It can do nothing else – closing is yours. Give it to the AI, for example as MOSCOOKBOOK_TASK_KEY.

Tokens.title: Token usage
Tokens.intro: What the AI calls used in the last 30 days, what for – and above all, how to use less. Counted in tokens, the way the provider bills; your provider shows the price per token.
Tokens.splitHint: Written tokens usually cost 4–5× what read ones do.
Tokens.empty: No AI calls counted yet. Counting starts with this update.

noRecipe.title: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} without a recipe {count, plural, one {was} other {were}} read with AI
noRecipe.do: The recipe was in the bio, the comments or sent by DM – no AI finds anything there. Delete such items right away, or open the source and share the link to the recipe page.

repeats.title: {count, plural, one {# item was} other {# items were}} read with AI 3 times or more
repeats.do: After “rules plus AI”, “Read with AI” gives the same answer. Read again for free first, then “Read with AI only” at most once – otherwise finish it by hand.

learnSite.title: Sites read with AI more than once: {detail}
learnSite.do: Teach them in advance under Admin → AI → Learned sites. Imports from there then need no AI.

videos.title: YouTube costs {detail}× what other sources do
videos.do: Subtitles are long. If the video description links to the recipe, share that link instead – web pages are usually read for free.

aiOnly.title: “Read with AI only” costs {detail}× “Read with AI”
aiOnly.do: It sends everything that was shared. Only use it when “rules plus AI” was clearly wrong.

smallerModel.title: A large model does most of the work: {detail}
smallerModel.do: For recipes from text a small model is usually enough – a fraction of the price per token. Set the model under Admin → AI and compare a few imports; switch back if results get worse.

modeImages.title: The AI is asked automatically on every share
modeImages.do: With the “pictures only” setting (Admin → AI) the AI reads text and pages only when you press “Read with AI”. That saves the most.

fine.title: Nothing stands out
fine.do: No pattern worth saving on. The basic rules below still apply.

rules.free: Rules first: pages with recipe markup, cleanly written captions and notes cost nothing. The AI only comes in when that is not enough.
rules.link: Share the link to the recipe page rather than the post or video – pages are cheapest, videos with subtitles the most expensive.
rules.once: “Read again” is free. An item the AI has already read does not get better by asking again.
rules.mode: “Pictures only” is the most frugal setting: the AI then reads text only when you press the button.
rules.model: A small model costs a fraction of a large one per token and is usually enough for recipes.
rules.learn: Have sites you import from often learned once – after that, no AI needed.
